scope: Evidence map for the selected ISSI Rev F profile; not a complete JEDEC conformance claim.

classification_legend.direct_oracle: Independent Python predicate is exercised by a relevant event class in the generated Rust-controller trace. This means a selected trace path was checked, not that the threshold or all combinations were tested.
classification_legend.other_rust_boundary: A named Rust test asserts the rule boundary or a specific invalid state; the independent Python monitor does not cover it.
classification_legend.partial: A named Rust test or monitor guard covers only a related path/assumption, without isolating the ledger rule boundary or full state space.
classification_legend.untested: No named Rust boundary assertion or independent monitor guard was identified.
classification_legend.configuration_invariant: The selected profile/API fixes this condition as a configuration assumption and rejects unsupported configuration or command inputs. It is not an executed transition boundary; continuous ideal CK cannot represent an external clock stop or restart.

mutation_review.scope_note: Seven targeted rejection probes; these do not exhaustively mutate every one of the 77 ledger rows.

policy_notes: The idle refresh deadline check is the selected controller policy for this trace, whose request traffic finishes before its first refresh. It is intentionally stronger than the device postponement allowance and must not be described as JEDEC zero-debt.

The checker covers initialization, open-page commands, data windows and byte mapping, completion, and refresh. Power, training, raw auto-precharge, analog/electrical behavior, and many state interactions remain outside its independent scope.

The selected 834 ps profile supplies a continuous ideal CK from time zero. Clock-before-CKE, SRE clock hold, SRX clock setup, and selected clock-latency rows are configuration/API invariants; the suite rejects unsupported clock settings/commands but does not execute a clock-stop negative case.

The Vref one-code and multi-code waits are checked at 72 CK and 180 CK by named Rust assertions. The next-ACT early failure is reported through the generic VREF_enter readiness rule; training remains outside the independent Python monitor.

RDA/WRA-to-ACT and PD minimum behavior have positive and one-cycle-early Rust boundaries through composed/shared constraints. Their coverage classification does not require a unique surfaced guard name; they remain outside the independent Python monitor, and no checker/guard ordering was changed.
